subject: Entitlement seat-proxy mapping and fulfillment exceptions for SignalGrid (AWS Marketplace)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@signalgird.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@signalgird.com, aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify entitlement proxy pattern for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Hi Grace / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our Cloud Ops and Procurement teams as we start the AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment integration for SignalGrid's seat-based product:

- We use a seat-proxy model: customer instances connect to our service using a local seat token that maps to a single Hub license key on our side. For Marketplace fulfillment the buyer expects an entitlement per-account. How should we best map the proxy token to the Marketplace entitlement to avoid double-billing or missed invoicing?
- In the contract there is a requested exception for monthly seat reconciliation windows (SignalGrid wants a 72h reconciliation window vs the usual 24h). Procurement has included the exception in the attached PDF. Will that block fulfillment?
- If the metering webhook fails, what are Redwood's recommended retry/fallback paths to ensure Marketplace receives accurate usage?

I've attached our proposed mapping spreadsheet (SaaS_Entitlement_Mapping_v2.xlsx) and the contract exception PDF. Can we get an internal plan + ETA? We're aiming for activation before end of March.

Appreciate it,
Elena Torres
Head of Cloud Operations
SignalGrid

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@signalgird.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify entitlement proxy pattern for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. Looping in Priyom and Ben for the integration specifics, and Kimberly for the contract exception. Quick bullets from my side: 

- We can support mapping the seat proxy token to a single Marketplace entitlement ID per customer account. The common approach is: provision entitlement_id -> Redwood internal account_id -> map seat tokens as children that report usage against the entitlement_id.
- Reconciliation window exception: legal/ops will need to sign off. Kimberly, can you confirm if 72h would be acceptable from our Marketplace fulfillment perspective or if we need to preserve 24h for guaranteed invoice timing?
- For webhook failures: we recommend three retries with exponential backoff and a durable queue on your side; Redwood can accept batched backfill events for up to 30 days (subject to contract) — we should document the JSON payload and signature header so AWS/Redwood can correlate.

Action items:
1) Priyom: propose payload & backfill format + sample webhook file.
2) Kimberly: confirm contract exception impact and DocuSign flow.
3) Ben: confirm billing cadence expectations vs SignalGrid's invoicing.
4) Elena: confirm target date (end of March) or propose buffer.

I'll schedule a 30m technical sync for tomorrow to walk through the payload.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
[calendar invite sent]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@signalgird.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify entitlement proxy pattern for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Thanks — quick technical proposal (high level):

1) Entitlement mapping model
   - Marketplace entitlement_id (ent-XXX) created per SignalGrid account (customer principal).
   - Redwood stores a mapping table: entitlement_id -> account_id -> list(seat_token_ids). Seat tokens are ephemeral but have stable owner metadata that includes account_id.

2) Metering events and backfill
   - Primary path: seat proxies emit usage to SignalGrid backend -> SignalGrid aggregates per entitlement_id -> posts a metering event to Redwood's fulfillment API.
   - If real-time post fails, SignalGrid can batch usage and post a backfill file (JSON newline-delimited) up to 30 days. Redwood will verify signature and ingest, then forward to AWS SaaS fulfillment if requested.

3) Webhook schema (sample attachment: fulfillment-webhook-example.json)
   - {
     "entitlement_id": "ent-abc123",
     "account_id": "sg-account-456",
     "timestamp": "2027-02-25T17:00:00Z",
     "usage_amount": 42,
     "usage_unit": "seats",
     "origin_tokens": ["token-1", "token-2"]
   }

4) Failure & idempotency
   - Events must include a client_event_id for idempotency. Redwood will de-dupe events for 72h.
   - For missed events, backfill files should include the original client_event_id and timestamp.

Notes for procurement: if SignalGrid is authorised to post on behalf of accounts (proxy aggregation), we must ensure the contract explicitly allows aggregated reporting. Otherwise AWS may require per-user entitlements.

I've attached a minimal example payload and a small script we use to validate signatures. Happy to do a short demo in the sync.

Priyom Das
Senior Integration Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: procurement@signalgird.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify entitlement proxy pattern for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Elena / Grace,

I reviewed the contract exception PDF. Short answers: 

- 72h reconciliation window: we can accept the exception technically, but we need an explicit clause that SignalGrid will provide a daily reconciliation summary and accept potential billing adjustments that may be backdated for up to one billing cycle. That protects Redwood and AWS fulfillment flows.
- DocuSign: I pre-filled the amendment and sent a PowerForm link to SignalGrid procurement. Please sign the amendment that includes the reconciliation clause. Link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234-efgh

Procurement note: once signed, Redwood will configure the entitlement to accept 72h backfills and enable the 30-day batched ingestion mode. This will change the SLA for invoice finality; finance will be notified.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@signalgird.com>

Grace / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the meeting yesterday. Quick confirmation:

- We will adopt the mapping approach (entitlement_id per account + seat tokens reported as origin_tokens).
- Procurement signed the amendment this morning (see attached).
- We'll implement the batch backfill producer next week and push the first sample file by 2027-03-07.
- Proposed follow-up: Tue 2027-03-02 10:00 PT for final test. Calendar invite attached.

Appreciate the clarity — Priyom, we'll send the sample payload and the first backfill file to your testing endpoint.

Elena Torres
Head of Cloud Operations | SignalGrid
